claim: ARCHITECTURE.md sect.2 - 60 frames writing x and y adds 12,000 structs across 200 shapes
why: structural: a deterministic struct count, bit-identical across runs. Any change means Item.mergeWith behaviour changed and the one-hot-key rule needs revisiting.

claim: ARCHITECTURE.md sect.2 - the same 60 frames writing ONE transform key adds 200
why: structural, as above. This is the 60x that justifies geometry living in one key.

claim: ARCHITECTURE.md sect.10 - encodeStateAsUpdateV2 is 26.8x smaller than the append-only log, losslessly
why: structural: the simulation is deterministic and reproduced identically across two runs.

claim: ARCHITECTURE.md sect.7 - applyUpdate on a ~7.8MB blob is one uninterruptible task of ~2,027ms
why: timing, hardware- and load-bound: measured 1837.6ms on this machine against the documented 2027ms (9.4%). The claim is the order of magnitude - that a 50k-shape board costs seconds, not milliseconds - so the tolerance is deliberately wide.

claim: Phase 0 spike - moving a 50,000-shape OBJECT scene across a worker boundary costs ~261ms
why: timing, hardware-bound. The claim is the order of magnitude: an object scene costs hundreds of ms to cross, which is the same order as the decode a worker is meant to hide - so the transport must be typed arrays.
